newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas hits new highs late on Arctic weather.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas hits new highs late on Arctic weather.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures continued to hit highs late Monday in moderate activity, with forecasts for an Arctic blast later this week driving cash and futures sharply higher, industry sources said.

At 1435 EST, January was 66.9 cents higher at $4.52 per million British thermal units after surging late to another contract high and all-time high of $4.56. February, which also set another benchmark of $3.97, was up 53.5 cents at $3.93.
"Clearly, the weather is going to be well-below normal and that's driving us," said one East Coast trader, noting a lot of speculative length may be in the market.
Forecasters expect temperatures over most of the nation to plunge to 15 degrees F below-normal or colder, as an Arctic air mass from Canada sweeps into the Midwest.
And with the cold expected to hang around through the month, few expected a significant pullback near-term.

Technical traders said January resistance was difficult to peg, with the contract moving into uncharted territory today, but some saw next resistance in the $4.95 area based on a swing measurement. Support was seen in the low-to-mid $3.50s and then at $3.19.

In the cash, Gulf Coast prices surged about 40 cents to about the $4 level. Midcontinent pipes were at least 50 cents higher at about $4. Gas at the New York city gate was talked in the $4.40 area, also up almost 50 cents.
NYMEX said 32,115 contracts traded at 1410 EST. Hub open interest on Dec 13 rose 5,968 contracts to 156,270.
NYMEX Alberta and Permian natgas futures remained untraded at 1440 EST.

On the KCBT, January was 70 cents at $4.37 after hitting another new high of $4.40. February was 51.5 cents higher at $3.78, also a contract high. The East/West spread narrowed by 3.1 cents to 15.0 cents (NYMEX premium).
